data.title: BioETL Architecture Graph
data.description: Сетевой граф архитектуры репозитория BioETL: слои Hexagonal Architecture, medallion-поток данных, ключевые технологические опоры и сигналы топологии пакетов.

nodes.label: BioETL
nodes.description: Python ETL-платформа для сбора и нормализации bioactivity-данных из нескольких научных и биомедицинских провайдеров.

nodes.label: Hexagonal Architecture
nodes.description: Главный архитектурный принцип проекта: зависимости направлены через порты и адаптеры с жёсткими импортными границами между слоями.

nodes.label: Medallion Architecture
nodes.description: Поток данных организован по слоям Bronze, Silver и Gold для трассируемости, качества данных и управляемой эволюции схем.

nodes.label: Domain Layer
nodes.description: Слой чистой предметной логики: порты, сущности, value objects, сервисы, схемы и инварианты без I/O.

nodes.label: Application Layer
nodes.description: Слой оркестрации use case-ов, lifecycle, batch execution, pipeline execution и прикладных сервисов.

nodes.label: Infrastructure Layer
nodes.description: Слой адаптеров и технических реализаций: HTTP-клиенты, storage, config, observability, locking и quality tooling.

nodes.label: Composition Layer
nodes.description: Composition root и bootstrap-слой, в котором собираются runtime-граф зависимостей, фабрики и entrypoints.

nodes.label: Interfaces Layer
nodes.description: Граничный слой внешних интерфейсов, в основном CLI, HTTP health и ограниченные orchestration entrypoints.

nodes.label: Provider APIs
nodes.description: Внешние источники данных проекта: ChEMBL, PubChem, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, CrossRef, OpenAlex и UniProt.

nodes.label: Delta Lake
nodes.description: Базовая технология хранения Silver и Gold слоёв с ACID-транзакциями, merge/upsert semantics и schema enforcement.

nodes.label: Pandera
nodes.description: Слой датафрейм-валидации, который используется для schema validation и контроля качества на медальонных переходах.

nodes.label: Package Topology
nodes.description: Структурная картина пакетов репозитория, показывающая ширину и специализацию семейств в слоях системы.

nodes.label: Governance Signals
nodes.description: Набор evidence-сигналов, которые используются для интерпретации топологии и принятия решений о рефакторинге.

nodes.label: Configuration System
nodes.description: Иерархическая YAML-конфигурация пайплайнов, провайдеров, composite-режимов и quality-правил, пронизывающая runtime-сборку.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.description: Слой логирования, tracing и quality-сигналов, проходящий через application и infrastructure для контроля исполнения пайплайнов.

edges.description: BioETL depends on Hexagonal Architecture to separate business logic from technical adapters, enforce import boundaries, and keep runtime assembly explicit through ports and adapters.
BioETL depends on Medallion Architecture to move provider data from raw capture into normalized and curated analytical layers with traceable quality gates.
Hexagonal Architecture constrains Domain Layer to remain pure and free of I/O so that domain invariants, ports, entities, and value objects stay reusable and stable.
Hexagonal Architecture positions Application Layer as the orchestrator of use cases, where workflows call domain abstractions without importing concrete infrastructure adapters.
Hexagonal Architecture maps Infrastructure Layer to concrete adapters that implement ports for storage, HTTP access, configuration, locking, and observability concerns.
Hexagonal Architecture relies on Composition Layer to build object graphs, inject dependencies through constructors, and keep factory calls out of domain and application logic.
Hexagonal Architecture uses Interfaces Layer as the boundary where CLI and HTTP requests enter the system before being routed into composition and application services.
Provider APIs are consumed by Infrastructure Layer through HTTP clients and adapters, because external I/O is intentionally isolated from domain and application code.
Infrastructure Layer depends on Domain Layer for ports, types, exceptions, and schemas so that adapter implementations stay aligned with domain contracts.
Application Layer depends on Domain Layer for business rules, port contracts, and value semantics while coordinating pipeline execution and batch-level workflows.
Composition Layer assembles Application Layer services by wiring runners, lifecycle services, and provider-specific execution seams into a concrete runtime graph.
Composition Layer integrates Infrastructure Layer adapters into the runtime by selecting concrete storage, HTTP, config, and observability implementations for each workflow.
Interfaces Layer invokes Composition Layer entrypoints so that CLI and boundary handlers do not hard-code business-logic construction or service location patterns.
Medallion Architecture depends on Delta Lake for Silver and Gold persistence because the project standard requires transactional storage and controlled schema evolution.
Medallion Architecture uses Pandera to validate dataframe structure and quality at key transitions, especially when normalizing raw provider records into curated datasets.
Application Layer operationalizes Medallion Architecture through pipeline runners, lifecycle services, and batch execution flows that move data across Bronze, Silver, and Gold.
Configuration System drives Composition Layer because runtime assembly, provider selection, composite execution, and quality rules are resolved from hierarchical YAML inputs.
Configuration System is heavily implemented in Infrastructure Layer through config loaders, normalizers, schema adapters, and policy validation components.
Configuration System connects to Domain Layer through canonical config dataclasses and validation semantics that define stable meaning beyond file parsing concerns.
Observability in BioETL spans Application Layer through lifecycle events, pipeline observers, and tracing helpers that describe execution behavior without owning concrete sinks.
Observability depends on Infrastructure Layer for concrete logging, anomaly handling, and telemetry implementations that persist or emit the signals defined by the application.
Package Topology shows Domain Layer as one of the broadest surfaces, but BioETL evidence indicates that much of this breadth reflects specialization rather than uncontrolled drift.
Package Topology identifies Infrastructure Layer as broad and family-rich, especially around adapters, storage, config, and observability clusters that form meaningful structural groupings.
Package Topology highlights that Application Layer looks narrow by direct package count while hiding dense orchestration seams in core, pipelines, and lifecycle-heavy modules.
Package Topology shows Composition Layer as a compact but coordination-dense area where bootstrap runtime and pipeline factories carry disproportionate architectural weight.
Package Topology shows Interfaces Layer as intentionally narrow, which supports the interpretation that BioETL keeps delivery surfaces small and boundary-focused.
Governance Signals interpret Package Topology by telling BioETL where structural breadth is acceptable specialization and where it may justify targeted review or refactoring.
Governance Signals guide BioETL maintenance decisions by prioritizing dense families and evidence-backed hotspots instead of using raw package count as a blunt trigger.
Domain Layer connects to Pandera through schema definitions and validation semantics that express domain expectations for structured dataframe content.
Provider APIs feed Medallion Architecture because external records are first captured in Bronze and then progressively normalized and curated through later data layers.
